strategy.summary: The detail scenario in perf/orders.js (GET /orders/:id) slowed from a p95 of 22 ms to 91 ms and a p99 of 25 ms to 95 ms, and a rerun confirmed it. The bisect points to 62d8c6ffbfbb (PR #111), which awaits findProduct once per order line, one after another. Each call is a separate store round trip of 6–9 ms, and an order has 8 lines, so a request makes 8 extra queries. We add thresholds scoped to the detail scenario at the baseline plus 20%, record the defect, and file an issue.
inScope: p95 and p99 http_req_duration thresholds for the detail scenario in perf/orders.js
Recording and filing the detail-scenario regression
outOfScope: Changing application code to fix the slowdown (a person's job)
perf/search.js and the list scenario: neither was reported slow
Restructuring the existing script beyond adding the thresholds
assumptions: The thresholds use the baseline from the work item: the median of the last 5 good runs, p95 22 ms and p99 25 ms. With the run's 20% headroom they become p(95)<26.4 and p(99)<30.
The existing global thresholds (http_req_failed rate<0.01, http_req_duration p(95)<2000), both scenarios and both checks stay unchanged.
run_tests runs smoke mode with --no-thresholds, so the counted runs only prove the script still runs. The new thresholds will fail under real load until the N+1 is fixed, and that is the intent.

risks.description: A 26.4 ms p95 is tight on a CI runner that is slower than the baseline environment.
risks.mitigation: The limit comes from the measured baseline plus the threshold the run allows. A noisy runner shows as a failure a person can triage, not as a hidden regression.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The perf/orders.js detail scenario fails its thresholds when p95 http_req_duration is 26.4 ms or more, or p99 is 30 ms or more (the last good baseline of 22/25 ms plus 20%)

testCases.title: detail scenario holds p95 and p99 latency to the last good baseline
steps: Run perf/orders.js under its own load (20 req/s for 10 s per scenario)
testCases.expected: Thresholds pass at the baseline. With the N+1 product lookups added in 62d8c6ffbfbb (p95 about 91 ms), they fail.
testCases.testData: Orders 1–60, 8 lines each, from the in-memory store
testCases.rationale: Guards the detail-scenario p95 and p99 latency regression (22→91 ms, 25→95 ms). Commit 62d8c6ffbfbb (PR #111) awaits findProduct once per line, one after another, adding 8 store round trips of 6–9 ms each to every GET /orders/:id.

strategy.environmentNotes: The orders-api must be running at BASE_URL (default http://localhost:4310).

defects.title: GET /orders/:id makes one product query per line: detail p95 22→91 ms
defects.description: The perf/orders.js detail scenario (GET /orders/:id at 20 req/s) slowed past the 20% threshold. p95 went from 22 ms to 91 ms (+312.7%, 87 ms on the rerun). p99 went from 25 ms to 95 ms (+286.3%, 89 ms on the rerun). The baseline is the median of the last 5 good runs. The bisect found the first slow commit: 62d8c6ffbfbb "Show each line's product name on an order" (PR #111). It added `for (const line of items) line.productName = (await findProduct(line.productId)).name;` to src/app.js. Each findProduct call is one store round trip of 6–9 ms (src/store.js roundTrip), and the calls are awaited one after another. Every order has 8 lines, so each request makes 8 extra sequential queries, about 60 ms more, which matches the rise. A fix could return the product name from orderLines in its single query, as it already does for priceCents. New thresholds guard it in perf/orders.js: 'http_req_duration{scenario:detail}': ['p(95)<26.4', 'p(99)<30'].
defects.evidence: TestForge measurement: detail p95 22→91 ms (rerun 87), p99 25→95 ms (rerun 89). Bisected to 62d8c6ffbfbb. src/app.js awaits findProduct once per line in a for loop; src/store.js findProduct awaits roundTrip() (6 ms + up to 3 ms jitter).
